categories.name: Sample filter misstated
categories.definition: The code includes or drops observations based on their substantive values in a way the report does not disclose or explicitly denies, so the analyzed population differs from the one described.
categories.criterion: The disagreement is about which observations enter based on their observed values (a skin-tone range, a red-card requirement), not about missingness or how a variable is built.

categories.name: Exposure operationalized differently
categories.definition: The skin-tone predictor is binned, thresholded, dichotomized, or aggregated across raters differently than the report states, so the treatment variable itself is not what is claimed.
categories.criterion: The misdescribed quantity is the causal exposure (cutpoint value, dichotomization edge, rater sum-vs-average, latent-class coding); when a middle band is dropped as part of defining the exposure it belongs here, not in sample_composition.

categories.name: Adjustment set or covariate build wrong
categories.definition: Which control variables enter the model, how many levels a covariate has, or how a covariate is transformed differs from the report.
categories.criterion: The disagreement concerns control/adjustment variables (position, league, club, height/weight, goals, standardization) in an analysis both agree was run, not the exposure or the outcome.

categories.name: Outcome defined differently
categories.definition: The red-card dependent variable is constructed differently than reported, e.g. binarized when the report denies any transformation or excludes card types the report says were pooled.
categories.criterion: The misdescribed quantity is the outcome variable (binary vs count, which card types are counted).

categories.name: Missing-data handling wrong
categories.definition: Missing values are imputed by a different method, or dropped when the report claims imputation (or vice versa), or a different variable's missingness drives exclusions than reported.
categories.criterion: The disagreement hinges on how absent values are treated (impute method, drop-vs-keep, which variable's gaps cause loss), regardless of which variable is involved.

categories.name: Estimator or inference mislabeled
categories.definition: For an analysis both sources agree was run, the model family, link function, standard-error type, bootstrap type, estimand, or diagnostic is described incorrectly.
categories.criterion: Both sources agree the analysis exists and they disagree only on how it computes its estimate or uncertainty.

categories.name: Set of analyses run misstated
categories.definition: The report's account of what was investigated is false: it claims specifications or variables were explored that the code never runs, or it denies analyses (or calls them impossible) that the code performs.
categories.criterion: The disagreement is about whether an analysis, specification, or variable was used at all, not about the numeric details of an agreed analysis.

categories.name: Reason for a choice falsified
categories.definition: A modeling choice is presented as principled or substantive, but the code shows it was made because it produced the most favorable result.
categories.criterion: The disagreement is about why a choice was made rather than what the choice was.

categories.name: Reported numbers not computed
categories.definition: The code hardcodes reported estimates as literals, contradicting an explicit claim that all results are computed from the code or that nothing was fabricated.
categories.criterion: An explicit reproducibility or no-fabrication assertion is falsified by hand-entered literal values in the outputs.
